reply.text:
Good that you're checking it. Form cues I can give you, so let me pull up your deadlift history first to see what's been loading. Nothing's logged for deadlifts in the last twelve weeks, so I can't see your loads, but the cues themselves don't depend on that. Set up with the bar over mid-foot, shins nearly touching it, and your hips between your knees and a normal squat. Brace your gut hard before you pull, then push the floor away with your legs while keeping the bar close to your legs the whole way. Lock out by standing tall and squeezing your glutes, not by leaning back.

The two most common faults are the lower back rounding and the hips shooting up first, so if you can, film a set from the side and check whether your back stays flat and your hips and shoulders rise together. If the bar drifts away from you or you feel it in your lower back, drop the weight and rebuild with lighter sets. And if anything hurts rather than just feels hard, that's one for a doctor or physio, not me. Tell me what the messed-up part looks like, and I'll help you tighten it.
